intent: To demonstrate the proportion of taxes owed by Americans that remained unpaid between 2008 and 2010.

units.meaning: The share of taxes owed that remained unpaid was 18.3%.
accepted_routes: 18.3% of taxes owed were not paid
Unpaid taxes made up 18.3% of the total owed
units.visual_evidence_rule: A NOT PAID slice/segment labeled 18.3% (or rounded 18%) must be visible and should appear as less than half of the whole.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about taxes really owed; if narration adds an unpaid clause, it should carry this value.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly state the 18.3% unpaid share, or can it rely on the implied complement to the paid share?

units.meaning: The share of taxes owed that was paid was 81.7%.
accepted_routes: Taxes paid were 81.7% of the total owed
units.visual_evidence_rule: A TAXES PAID slice/segment labeled 81.7% (or rounded 82%) must be visible and should appear as the majority of the whole.
units.reviewer_question: Should the paid share be required context or only optional support for the unpaid proportion?

units.meaning: The paid and unpaid shares are complementary parts of the same whole and sum to 100%.
accepted_routes: The two shares sum to 100%: 81.7% paid + 18.3% unpaid
Paid and unpaid account for all taxes owed
The pie is split into 81.7% paid and 18.3% not paid
Together the categories make the full whole
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both slices must be shown as parts of one pie/whole representing all taxes owed; the whole should read as 100%.
units.temporal_anchor: the full paid-vs-owed statement; the unpaid share is the remainder.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show that the two slices account for 100% of taxes owed, or is the pie's whole implicit?

units.meaning: The paid share was much larger than the unpaid share; 81.7% is about 4.46 times 18.3%.
accepted_routes: Paid share was about 4.5 times the unpaid share
Paid was more than four times unpaid
Unpaid was about 22% of the paid share
The paid slice dominated the unpaid slice by a factor of roughly 4.5
units.visual_evidence_rule: The TAXES PAID slice must be visibly much larger than NOT PAID; if ratio text is used, it should be derived from the two shares, not presented as a table cell.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'only 81.7%' clause contrasted with the remaining unpaid share.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include an explicit paid-vs-unpaid comparison/ratio, or is showing the two slices enough?

optional_valid: Show a legend/color key for NOT PAID and TAXES PAID.
Round 81.7% to 82% and 18.3% to 18% for readability.
Animate the unpaid slice as the remainder after the paid slice.
Use a pie chart total of 100% of taxes owed.
unsupported_to_avoid: Dollar amounts of taxes owed or unpaid (not in the table).
Causal claims that IRS enforcement, policy, or economic conditions caused the unpaid share.
Extrapolating to years outside the clip or trends across years; the table has only one pie.
Saying unpaid was 18.3% of paid (wrong denominator; if derived, it is 18.3/81.7 ≈ 22.4% of paid).
Treating 18.3% and 81.7% as counts or dollar values rather than shares of taxes owed.
notes: Intent focuses on unpaid 18.3%; narration leads with paid 81.7%, so the paid complement is marked optional unless the reviewer requires full pie composition. The period context is in the intent/narration but not the table, so it is not used as a numeric basis unit.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
